changelog: Fix: migrations/2026_09_25_0001_create_backtest_tables.sql and migrations/2026_09_25_0002_add_backtest_session_name.sql both used "ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS", which is MariaDB-only syntax -- MySQL (8.0 and 8.4 both) has no such clause and rejects it outright with ERROR 1064. This is very likely the real root cause behind the v3.20.2 "Loading forever" investigation: the old Namecheap host ran MariaDB, where this syntax silently worked; the new Hetzner host (migrated 2026-09-24) runs real MySQL 8.4, where it has never worked. Both files now use an information_schema.COLUMNS existence check + PREPARE/EXECUTE to build and run the ALTER only when the column is actually missing -- the same pattern this project already used correctly for the FK-exists check in the same file, generalized to columns. Verified directly against migrate.php's own splitSqlStatements() tokenizer (a hand-rolled parser that only understands backslash-escaped quotes, not the SQL-standard doubled-quote escape) before shipping, not assumed from standard SQL rules.

Audited every other file in app/migrations/ for the same MariaDB-only conditional-DDL clauses (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS, ADD INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, DROP INDEX IF EXISTS) -- none found elsewhere. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is standard SQL and untouched; it was never the problem.

Both corrected files are safe to re-run against the live database's current partially-applied state: backtest_sessions already exists there (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS no-ops on it), trades.backtest_session_id and the fk_trades_backtest_session constraint do not yet exist (the information_schema checks will find them missing and add them), and backtest_pending_orders does not yet exist either (creates cleanly). 2026_09_25_0002 never reached live at all (0001 failed first and stopped the runner in filename order), so it's a fresh first run either way.

Docs: CLAUDE.md's Server Environment section now states MySQL 8.4 explicitly (not just "MySQL") and explains the MariaDB-only conditional-ALTER trap directly, with the information_schema-check + PREPARE/EXECUTE pattern as the required replacement going forward. The migration-authoring checklist in §3A gained the same rule as its own numbered step.
release_notes: Code-only release (both changed files are migration SQL, corrected in place since 2026_09_25_0001 is still status='failed' on live and 2026_09_25_0002 never ran -- both are retryable per this project's own checksum-lock rule, which only applies to applied/baselined rows). Per instruction, migrations were NOT run and nothing was deployed as part of this turn. After Update Now, run migrate.php?mode=status to confirm both files show as pending/failed-and-retryable, then migrate.php?mode=run to apply them. This is expected to be the actual fix for the "Loading forever" symptom investigated in v3.20.2 -- get_backtest_sessions can only succeed once backtest_sessions (already there) AND trades.backtest_session_id AND the FK all exist, and the ALTER that creates the column has been failing outright until this release.
